newsitem.title: USA: Applied Materials stands by Q4 forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Applied Materials stands by Q4 forecasts.

text.p: Applied Materials Inc still expects fourth quarter earnings of about $0.48 a share before a one-time charge of about $0.10 to cover costs of a restructuring begun this summer, Chief Financial Officer Gerald Taylor said on Tuesday.
Applied Materials also still expects fourth quarter revenues of about $850 million and fourth quarter orders of about $700 million, Taylor told the Montgomery Securities Investment Conference.
He predicted the downturn in the semiconductor equipment industry would last at least "several more quarters."
Applied Materials provided the same fourth quarter earnings and revenue forecasts in a conference call with analysts in August.
In the third quarter the company earned $0.92 a share on revenues of $1.115 billion.
Taylor said the downturn in the semiconductor equipment industry surfaced in July and would cause "a dip," encompassing part of 1996 and part of 1997, in the industry's otherwise fast growth.
Applied Materials expects fast growth to resume by 1998.
It estimates today's $17 billion market for semiconductor equipment will grow to $30 billion by the year 2000, Taylor said.

He said the "dip" resulted mostly from overzealous DRAM production. Once the glut of DRAM inventory and production capacity is evened out, the DRAM market will grow 60 to 70 percent a year in terms of demand for bits of memory, he said.
"So the good news is, this will work itself out," Taylor told the investment group.
As the largest chip equipment company, providing processing technology for every step of the semiconductor manufacturing process, Applied Materials is very well positioned, he said.

Its worldwide operations are a big advantage, he said. "In the equipment industry you have to be global. By the year 2000, production of ICs (integrated circuits) in Asia will be larger than production of semiconductors or ICs in the U.S. and Europe combined," Taylor said.
